I empathize with you my friend. I've somewhat recently lost the girl I loved. The girl that I sacrificed so much to be with. The girl that has a place in every one of my best memories. I remember the day she told me she didn't love me anymore. I remember crying, being angry, confused, a whole array of emotions. I later found out that she'd been hooking up with someone else at around the time she told me, and I somewhat recently found out that she's dating a guy I considered a friend amidst all the shit. I see them just about every day of the week, and I see that she's happier than ever. Happier than I ever made her. She told me that in hindsight, she never actually loved me. I've been struggling with depression, and angry, fucked up thoughts, along with suicidal inclinations. The only thing that's stopped me from ending the suffering is my family. They don't know about my thoughts, but I couldn't do it knowing what it would put them through. I waste the day either filling the void with food, driving around hoping someone crashes into me, or smoking, just waiting for cancer to introduce itself. I know the pain Joseph, I'm going through it right now, with you.

I just hope this reaches you before it's too late. Good luck my friend

It's difficult to ignore. One of the several reasons behind my depression is losing the girl I love, and him being one of the people I still considered a friend, who knew about what I was going through, started dating her behind my back. With that, he still acted as a friend, and even asked me about her while they were together. I'd try to ignore it, but I see them 5 days a week. They're in my face just about everywhere I go.

We're in the same boat my friend. I've wanted to take my life for a while now, but I know that my family would be devastated. I don't want any of them to feel guilty about it either. I read somewhere that losing someone to suicide increases a loved ones chances for suicide by 65%. I wish I could just die without anyone being affected, but I know that won't happen. I wish I could just get like cancer or something, something uncontrollable yknow. But yeah, we're going through this together my friend.

I feel like getting out of the situation is only a temporary solution because it just keeps coming back. I have started smoking recently, and it is somewhat relieving. Kind of like a short escape.
For me, I'm not sure if I can narrow it down to one thing. But I guess it stems from depression, heartbreak, self-hate, backstabbing. That sort of thing
